- If sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to match sentiment momentum.  
- If sentiment is strongly bearish (≤ -0.50) in recent days, model tends to overreact — reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overcorrects — cap forecast rise to 2–3% below peak or adjust downward 1–2 days.  
- Model consistently underestimates true price peaks in early 30d horizon — add 1–2% buffer to forecast for high sentiment + high recent price action.  
- Model often fails to capture mean reversion in 30d horizon — if sentiment is mixed or neutral, forecast should be slightly below recent 10d average.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag — forecast should be 1–2 days ahead of sentiment shift.  
- For 30d forecasts, if true outcome shows early sharp rise followed by decline, model often misses the peak — adjust forecast to peak at 3–5 days earlier than model.
